title: Find the Value Filling Half the Array
statement:
You get an array nums of length 2n. It holds exactly n + 1 different values: one of them appears exactly n times, and each of the other n values appears once.

Return the value that appears n times.

examples.why: n = 2: the 7 appears twice, 3 and 1 once each.
n = 3: three 5s and three different singles.
The two copies sit at the two ends, three places apart. Checking only neighbors or every second position would miss them.

constraints: One value appears n times, the other n values are distinct
hints: Every value except one appears once. What is special about the first value you meet for the second time?
A set of seen values finds it in one pass.
Without extra memory: n copies in 2n slots cannot all be far apart. Show that two copies are always at most 3 positions from each other, then compare each element with the next three.

explain.intuition:
Only one value repeats, so the first value you see twice is the answer. A set of values seen so far finds it in one pass, like de-duplicating a list of ids.

There is also an O(1)-memory trick. Half the slots hold the same value. If every two copies were at least 4 positions apart, n copies would need about 4n − 3 slots, more than 2n once n ≥ 2. So some two copies are within distance 3 of each other, and comparing each nums[i] with nums[i + 1], nums[i + 2] and nums[i + 3] is enough.
steps: Walk through nums with a set of values seen so far.
If the current value is already in the set, return it.
Constant-memory variant: for gaps 1, 2, 3 and every i, return nums[i] when it equals nums[i + gap].
pitfalls: Checking only adjacent pairs: [4, 1, 2, 4] has its copies three apart.
Sorting and returning nums[n]. The block of copies always covers position n − 1 or n, but not always both (sorted [1, 1, 5, 6] has a 5 at position n), and sorting costs O(n log n) for nothing.
Counting all frequencies then searching for exactly n is fine but does twice the work; stopping at the first repeat is enough.

complexity.space: O(n) with a set, O(1) with the distance check

solutions.title: Compare every pair
solutions.idea: The only value that equals another element is the answer.

solutions.title: Set of seen values
solutions.idea: Return the first value that shows up a second time.

solutions.title: Copies are at most 3 apart
solutions.idea: By counting, some two copies sit within distance 3; check gaps 1, 2 and 3.

followups: The repeated value fills more than half the array but the others may also repeat. Which voting algorithm finds it in O(1) memory?
Prove the distance-3 bound. Is 3 tight?
